VideoGame Platform Learning MVP API (5.15.0)

Download OpenAPI specification:

Browser-facing API for the approved learning MVP vertical slice.

Provider-independent, same-origin contract for release discovery, a month's release calendar, weekly and monthly featured releases, the player-rating game ranking, bounded-catalogue search, the catalogue of one platform, the most anticipated upcoming releases of one platform, public game details, the selectable platform taxonomy, BFF session discovery, the authenticated user's ratings, rating statistics and preferred platforms, and the catalogue operator's synchronization status, coverage, bounded and historical synchronization requests, the stop or abandonment of one run, catalogue translation coverage and execution controls, and editorial anticipation lists. It contains the approved method/path operations, including private profile, data export and deletion.

Authentication navigation under /auth and the management-port synchronization, repair and localization commands are separate BFF and operational boundaries and are intentionally not exposed here. Provider image binaries are loaded from an approved CDN reference or replaced by a product-owned fallback; this API does not copy, proxy, or redistribute them.

Feedback

Anonymous visitor feedback handed to the configured receiving channel.

Submit visitor feedback

Anonymous JSON command with no query parameters. Cookies and identity are irrelevant. Cross-origin browser requests are rejected. The JSON request is limited to 32 KiB. A 204 means the configured SMTP receiver accepted the message, not that it reached an inbox or was read. The client never replays automatically. If acceptance is unconfirmed after a timeout or connection loss, a manual retry may send a second copy.

Request Body schema: application/json
required
category
required
string
Enum: "suggestion" "bug" "incorrect_game_information" "other"
message
required
string [ 1 .. 2000 ] characters

Plain text with at least one non-whitespace character. No attachments.

email
string <email> <= 254 characters

Optional single ASCII email address with a dot-atom local part and a fully qualified DNS domain. Omit when absent.

Download my complete supported personal data

One UTF-8 JSON attachment with format gameometro-personal-data-export, version 1, exportedAt, account (available session-validated name/email), ratings (gameId, title, direct value, played platforms with platformId/name/optional value, createdAt/updatedAt), and preferredPlatforms (configured, savedAt when configured, platforms). No credentials, tokens, provider payloads or other users' data. Reads one consistent local snapshot. Preparation is bounded to 10000 ratings, 16 MiB and 30 seconds; budget or source failure returns an error before any successful download, never a truncated successful export. Empty collections are valid. No query parameters are accepted.

Confirm and request deletion of my account

Requires literal ELIMINAR confirmation, same-origin CSRF and validated original OIDC auth_time within five minutes (missing/future time is refused). No user selector. Atomically records one intent per principal and blocks authenticated access. An automatic protected polling executor reuses the independent two-copy ledger and legal archive erasure engine. Admission requires explicit enablement and fresh authenticated executor readiness; otherwise 503 changes nothing. 202 means pending, never erased, and ends the requesting BFF session immediately. Completion requires verified absence and, in production, independent durable evidence. Retries preserve the same intent. A fixed receipt cookie permits status reads after session invalidation, expires after 24 hours and cannot authorize any mutation.

Historical synchronization

Operator-controlled durable calendar-month backfill.

Read durable historical synchronization progress

Operator-only, local durable evidence. Commands require session-bound CSRF proof. Calendar months are processed sequentially through ordinary reconciliation; first and last months are clipped to the inclusive requested dates (1950 through 2099). Completed months include deliberately skipped covered months. Completion does not imply error-free acquisition of every Game. Empty completed months are checkpointed. Counters total completed attempts only, excluding skipped months and failed attempts; they count processing, not distinct catalogue identities across months. A new target cannot replace unfinished work. Resume is explicit, including after restart. No startup action resumes provider work. Scheduled runs take priority between months. Read status after an ambiguous command before repeating it. No completion estimate.

Start, stop or resume catalogue translation

Requires session-bound CSRF proof. A command applies to the observed execution ID, omitted only before the first run. Acceptance does not imply completion. Stop takes effect between batches. Resume continues from the checkpoint after a stop or interruption, including a pause after a failed batch. If a pass ended with unresolved failures, resume begins a new pass that skips current content. Application startup never resumes an execution.

Releases

Public release exploration over an inclusive date range.

Explore the releases of an inclusive date range grouped by game

Reads a bounded page of games from the last valid local catalogue publication whose releases fall in an inclusive date range. Without from and to, the range is the current calendar week, Monday to Sunday, derived by the application in Europe/Madrid; the response states the evaluation date and the evaluated range. Each game appears once with only the releases that match the range and active filters, presenting at most one of them per platform (see ReleaseItem); page.totalItems counts games, not releases.

Days up to and including the evaluation date hold what has happened: a release with an exact day inside the range, or with a month, quarter or year period that has ended and overlaps the range, neither cancelled nor delayed. Later days hold what is expected: a release with an exact day inside the range that is not cancelled. A month, quarter or year period that has not ended joins, not cancelled, only with includeApproximateDates=true and only when it overlaps the range from the evaluation date on. A release with an unknown (TBA) date never belongs to a range. No release receives an invented day, and each keeps its real precision.

Platform and region filters are multi-select: values within one dimension combine with OR and the two dimensions combine with AND. availableFilters is contextual and faceted: platform options reflect the current range and the active region selection (never restricted by the active platform set), region options reflect the current range and the active platform selection (never restricted by the active region set), and a currently selected valid value always stays representable. sort orders the games before pagination, by date, attention (hype), community score or external player score; every order reads local state only and never calls a provider. Empty, review-required, imprecise-date and fallback-cover results are valid states. PostgreSQL groups by game, applies the range and filters, distinct facet discovery, presented-release selection, total ordering, count, limit, and offset before any release page reaches the application.

Since 4.0.0, from, to and sort replace the view and weeks parameters, which are now unknown parameters, and the response no longer carries view. Migration: a former recent window is to = today with from 7 × weeks − 1 days earlier, a former upcoming window runs from today; the order is now one ascending date order whatever the range.

query Parameters
from
string <date>
Example: from=2026-08-01

First day of the inclusive release-date range, an ISO calendar date. Send it together with to; omit both for the current calendar week, Monday to Sunday in Europe/Madrid. Sending only one of them yields 422 FILTER_INVALID for the missing one.

to
string <date>
Example: to=2026-08-31

Last day of the inclusive range. It must not precede from, and the range spans at most 92 days; otherwise the request yields 422 FILTER_INVALID for /query/to. A range may lie in the past, in the future or around the evaluation date, and may be a single day.

sort
string (ReleaseSort)
Default: "releaseDate"
Enum: "releaseDate" "hype" "rating" "externalPlayerScore"
Example: sort=hype

The order of the games, applied before pagination; every order ends in the unique gameId. releaseDate is ascending by each game's first presented release: the last day of its known period (the day itself for an exact date), an exact day before a month, quarter or year period ending the same day, then the case-insensitive canonical title. hype puts the highest release attention first; only a game with a launch in the range (a release whose stage is full_release or unknown) has attention, and a game first launched before from is a re-release, the order Destacados ranks with, whose value is never exposed. Since 5.14.0 attention is computed over the requested range's candidates: the mean of locally stored IGDB Hypes, Want to Play and Visits, each on a log scale relative to the strongest candidate (a remake, remaster, port or expanded game may claim half of its parent product's signal; a game first released before from keeps half of its own), averaged with the 1–100 score of the game in the operator's editorial anticipation list covering the range. The name hype is kept so existing links keep working. rating puts the highest Gameómetro community mean, at the one decimal shown, first, then the larger number of ratings. externalPlayerScore puts the highest locally stored external player score (currently IGDB players), at the one decimal of its /10 ExternalPlayerScore value, first, then the larger number of that source's ratings. A game without the chosen signal follows every game with one and is never treated as zero; ties continue with the releaseDate order.

includeApproximateDates
boolean
Default: false
Example: includeApproximateDates=true

Opt-in for the part of the range from the evaluation date on. Omitted or false, a release there appears only with an exact day. true also admits a month, quarter or year period that has not ended and overlaps that part; each keeps its real precision. Unknown (TBA) dates never join. Days before the evaluation date are unaffected, so the value changes nothing for a range that ends before it.

platformIds
Array of strings (PlatformId) unique [ items [ 1 .. 100 ] characters ]
Example: platformIds=platform_ps5&platformIds=platform_switch

Repeatable multi-select platform filter (platformIds=a&platformIds=b). Values in this dimension combine with OR; the platform and region dimensions combine with AND. Omit it for no platform filter. Values are trimmed and de-duplicated; an unknown value yields 422.

regionIds
Array of strings (RegionId) unique [ items [ 1 .. 100 ] characters ]
Example: regionIds=region_europe&regionIds=region_worldwide

Repeatable multi-select region filter (regionIds=a&regionIds=b). Values in this dimension combine with OR; the platform and region dimensions combine with AND. Omit it for no region filter, which is distinct from selecting the concrete Worldwide region. Values are trimmed and de-duplicated; an unknown value yields 422.

page
integer >= 1
Default: 1
Example: page=1

One-based page; a page beyond the last returns an empty page.

pageSize
integer [ 1 .. 100 ]
Default: 20
Example: pageSize=20
header Parameters
If-None-Match
string
Example: "catalogue-version-opaque"

Opaque public representation tag for a conditional read.

Release calendar

Public per-day release counts of one calendar month, from the current month on.

Count highlighted games releasing on each day of one calendar month

Reads, from the last valid local catalogue publication, how many games release on each day of one calendar month, for a monthly calendar. Without month the current month in Europe/Madrid is served. Navigation never goes back: a month must lie between the current month and the operator's months-forward bound (UC-024, 5 by default), the same forward bound featured months use; the current month is always accepted. The bound never states that the local catalogue is complete. presentation carries the operator's interest thresholds and day preview size.

This is the highlights calendar: only games with locally stored IGDB Hypes at or above the operator's minimum (10 by default) launching that day qualify; missing or lower Hype is excluded, and since 5.14.0 an early access, advance access, beta or alpha release is never counted or coloured (only a stage of full_release or unknown is a launch). The threshold is fixed, not a percentile recomputed per request. It filters contextual facets as well as day counts.

The calendar is active from the evaluation date on: days of the month before it are never counted. A day holds only releases with that exact day, under the release explorer's own rules (GET /releases): never cancelled, and on the evaluation date not delayed either. days lists each day from the evaluation date (or the month's first day, for a later month) to the month's last day holding at least one such release that matches the active filters, in ascending order; a day without one is absent. totalHype is the sum of local Hypes of the qualifying games on that day, counting each game once regardless of how many matching platforms or regions it has. The sum uses the same active filters as gameCount and excludes games below the highlights threshold. gameCount counts games, not releases: a game releasing on several platforms or regions that day counts once. The full explorer lists every qualifying release of that day without a highlights restriction, so its page.totalItems may exceed the calendar's gameCount. The calendar preview reads the leading games from GET /releases with sort=hype and a page size capped by both three and the day's highlighted-game count.

A release known only to its month, quarter or year, or with an unknown (TBA) date, never belongs to a day and is not counted; nothing is attributed to an invented day or month.

Platform and region filters, activeFilters and the contextual, faceted availableFilters follow GET /releases, evaluated over every release the calendar counts. PostgreSQL applies the filters, groups and counts; the response holds at most 31 days, and no game page is read. No provider is called, and the representation never varies on a session.

query Parameters
month
string (CalendarMonth) ^(?!0000)[0-9]{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])$
Examples: month=2026-10

Calendar month to count as YYYY-MM; omit it for the current month in Europe/Madrid. It must lie between the current month and the operator's months forward (5 by default) after it; the current month is always accepted. A malformed month or a month outside the bounds, including any earlier month, yields 422 FILTER_INVALID for /query/month.

platformIds
Array of strings (PlatformId) unique [ items [ 1 .. 100 ] characters ]
Example: platformIds=platform_ps5&platformIds=platform_switch

Repeatable multi-select platform filter (platformIds=a&platformIds=b). Values in this dimension combine with OR; the platform and region dimensions combine with AND. Omit it for no platform filter. Values are trimmed and de-duplicated; an unknown value yields 422.

regionIds
Array of strings (RegionId) unique [ items [ 1 .. 100 ] characters ]
Example: regionIds=region_europe&regionIds=region_worldwide

Repeatable multi-select region filter (regionIds=a&regionIds=b). Values in this dimension combine with OR; the platform and region dimensions combine with AND. Omit it for no region filter, which is distinct from selecting the concrete Worldwide region. Values are trimmed and de-duplicated; an unknown value yields 422.

Featured releases

Public automatic selection of a calendar week's or month's featured releases.

Read the automatic featured releases of one calendar week or month

Reads the automatic selection of one calendar period from the last valid local catalogue: an ISO 8601 week, Monday to Sunday, or a calendar month.

Since 5.9.0 the selection is the head of the release explorer: for the same period and platforms, the items are the first games of GET /releases with from and to set to the period's window, sort=hype and approximate dates left out, in the same order, each presenting the same releases and date, counting only games with release attention (ReleaseSort hype). Since 5.14.0 only a launch gives a game attention: a release whose stage is full_release or unknown in the period. Early access, advance access, betas and alphas never feature, although the explorer still lists them. Ports, remakes and editions take part whatever the game's first release was. Candidates rank by attention descending (since 5.14.0), then the releaseDate order, whose last key is the unique gameId. A game without any attention signal stays a normal catalogue and discovery result but is not ranked, and no value is ever invented. The first item is the period's featured release and up to five more follow; fewer items are returned rather than filling slots. Clients should expect a port as the featured release; a featured game may still present an early or advance access release on another platform beside its launch, so read each stage. Attention combines provider-observed interest with the operator's editorial anticipation list for the period; it never measures quality or a rating, and its value is not exposed. The application derives the evaluation date, the current week and the current month in Europe/Madrid. Without parameters the current calendar month is served. Any period inside the navigation bounds may be selected; it is ranked with the same current local popularity evidence, because no popularity history is kept. The navigation bounds and the attention weights are operator product settings (UC-024): by default weeks reach 16 weeks before and after the current week, and months reach 10 calendar months back, across years, and 5 forward. The bounds never state that the local catalogue is complete. navigation names the adjacent periods inside these bounds. PostgreSQL selects the qualifying releases, ranks and limits the games, and presents at most one release per platform before anything reaches the application. Each item also carries the landscape context-selected image and optional decorative secondary-card logo, chosen from locally stored provider media metadata and delivered as approved direct CDN references (ADR-0001). Up to two product-owned localized genres accompany each item; only the first item carries the existing localized summary representation. All content is served from PostgreSQL; no provider or translator is called.

Since 4.1.0, platformIds restricts the candidates before they are ranked: only a qualifying release on one of the named platforms makes its game a candidate, and each item presents only those releases. The ranking, its limit and its tie-breaker are unchanged, so a restricted selection is the ranking of the restricted candidates, never a filtered copy of the unrestricted six. The selection states no_qualifying_releases when none of the named platforms has a qualifying release in the period. Without platformIds the selection is unchanged. The representation depends only on the request's explicit parameters, never on a session.

query Parameters
granularity
string (FeaturedGranularity)
Enum: "week" "month"
Example: granularity=week

Period granularity. Omitted, it is week when week is present and month otherwise, so a request without parameters keeps serving the current calendar month. Without a period parameter of its own, it selects the current week or month in Europe/Madrid. Combining it with the other granularity's period parameter yields 422 FILTER_INVALID for that parameter.

week
string (IsoWeek) ^(?!0000)[0-9]{4}-W(0[1-9]|[1-4][0-9]|5[0-3])...
Examples: week=2026-W42

ISO 8601 week to feature as YYYY-Www, Monday to Sunday; YYYY is the week-based year, so 2026-W53 runs from 28 December 2026 to 3 January 2027. It must lie within the operator's weeks back and forward (16 by default) of the current week in Europe/Madrid. A malformed week, week 53 of a year with 52 weeks, a week outside the bounds, or a week combined with month or granularity=month yields 422 FILTER_INVALID for /query/week.

month
string (CalendarMonth) ^(?!0000)[0-9]{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])$
Examples: month=2026-10

Calendar month to feature as YYYY-MM. It must lie between the operator's months back (10 by default) before the current month in Europe/Madrid, across years, and the operator's months forward (5 by default) after it; the current month is always accepted. A malformed month, a month outside the bounds, or a month combined with granularity=week yields 422 FILTER_INVALID for /query/month.

platformIds
Array of strings (PlatformId) <= 50 items unique [ items [ 1 .. 100 ] characters ]
Example: platformIds=platform_ps5&platformIds=platform_switch2

Repeatable platform restriction (platformIds=a&platformIds=b) applied before ranking: values combine with OR. Omit it for every platform. Values are trimmed and de-duplicated; an unknown value yields 422 PLATFORM_NOT_SUPPORTED.

Catalogue

Public reads from the bounded local catalogue.

Search the bounded catalogue

Searches canonical titles and approved aliases after trimming. Matching is case- and diacritic-insensitive, requires every token, and is non-fuzzy. It never calls a provider. Zero and multiple matches are valid outcomes. Each result carries a bounded releaseContext sample and a separate releaseSummary computed from every locally stored release of that game, plus the scores of only the returned page's games, read from local state after matching, ranking and paging.

query Parameters
q
required
string [ 1 .. 100 ] characters .*\S.*
Example: q=resident evil 4

Trimmed query containing 1 to 100 Unicode code points.

page
integer >= 1
Default: 1
Example: page=1

One-based page; a page beyond the last returns an empty page.

pageSize
integer [ 1 .. 100 ]
Default: 20
Example: pageSize=20
header Parameters
If-None-Match
string
Example: "catalogue-version-opaque"

Opaque public representation tag for a conditional read.

Read public game details

Never varies by session or embeds a personal rating. Unavailable aggregate statistics and fallback covers are explicit degraded states in a coherent 200. Available statistics carry the per-platform community readings beside the one-vote-per-user Gameómetro mean; the validator covers both. The Game's own external player score is optional local evidence; its absence is not a degraded state. The validator covers it, so every reuse reflects its refresh or removal.

List the catalogue platforms a visitor may choose

Reads the platforms of the local, provider-independent taxonomy that at least one current release of the last valid catalogue publication uses, ordered by name, case-insensitively, then by platformId. These are the choices offered as preferred platforms; a platform no current release uses could never narrow release discovery, so it is not offered. The taxonomy is bounded and every platform is returned in one response; the read fails rather than truncating it. All content is served from PostgreSQL; no provider is called.

Ratings

Current-user personal-rating reads and commands.

Read personal rating statistics

UC-015. One repeatable-read snapshot of only the authenticated principal's current active ratings and Ratings-owned projected local genre/game context. No query inputs, external/community scores or provider access. Fixed-size aggregates, never a full history. Each rated game contributes its one personal contribution: the direct score, or the unrounded mean of its scored platforms. All means use the unrounded contributions and round half up to one decimal only for presentation. The distribution places each game once, in the bucket of its contribution rounded half up to the nearest integer (8.5 counts as 9), so bucket counts sum to the total while the mean stays exact. A genre receives one full contribution for every rated game assigned to it, so genre counts overlap; games without genres are counted separately. Genre lists hold at most six entries: most rated by count descending then genreId ascending; best rated (at least three games) by unrounded mean descending, count descending then genreId ascending. Extremes compare unrounded contributions; ties select gameId ascending and count every game with exactly that contribution. Activity is twelve calendar months ending in evaluatedOn's month in Europe/Madrid, counting surviving ratings by original creation time; edits do not move a contribution and deletion removes it. It is not a historical score or playing log. Platforms read only the played platforms the user recorded on current ratings, never Catalogue releases, preferred platforms or devices; see PersonalPlatformInsights.

Read, search, sort, and page Mis puntuaciones

Applies authenticated-current-user scope before search, sorting, counts, or pagination. Only active game ratings are returned. Search uses the catalogue's case- and diacritic-insensitive all-token word-prefix rules for canonical titles and approved aliases. Every sort ends with gameId ascending as its unique tie-breaker; ratingValue orders by each rating's unrounded contribution. Each item's entityTag is the current strong rating validator for conditional update and delete; it is not a collection cache validator. Community and external scores are read afterwards for only the selected page's Games.

Create or update the current user's rating

Creation requires If-None-Match: *; update requires current If-Match. Exactly one intent precondition is allowed. Eligibility is re-evaluated with the trusted application clock.

The command states the rating's score and, optionally, its played platforms. A rating has exactly one score source, so the user always casts one community vote: value is the direct score and is required exactly when no resulting platform carries a score; otherwise the contribution is the arithmetic mean of the scored platforms and value must be absent. platforms, when present, replaces the whole played-platform set (an empty array clears it); absent or null keeps the saved set unchanged, so a command with only value never touches saved platforms. A newly named platform must be one of the game's current release platforms; a platform already saved on the rating stays valid even if catalogue evidence later changes. The command is atomic: an invalid platform, score or precondition changes nothing.

Authorizations:
sessionCookie
path Parameters
gameId
required
string (GameId) [ 1 .. 100 ] characters
Examples: game_example

Opaque, provider-independent product game identifier.

header Parameters
X-CSRF-Token
required
string non-empty
Example: opaque-csrf-token

Session-bound anti-forgery token obtained from /session.

If-None-Match
string
Example: *

Must be * for create and cannot be combined with If-Match.

Value: "*"
If-Match
string (StrongEntityTag) >= 3 characters ^"[^"\r\n]+"$
Examples: "rating-version-opaque"

Required for update and cannot be combined with If-None-Match.

Request Body schema: application/json
required
value
integer [ 1 .. 10 ]

The direct score. Required exactly when no resulting platform carries a score; must be absent when one does.

Array of objects or null (RatingPlatformWrite) <= 50 items

When present, the complete set of played platforms, replacing the saved one; an empty array clears it. Absent or null keeps the saved set. Platform identifiers are unique.

Rankings

Public player-rating rankings of the released games in the local catalogue (TOPómetro), one source at a time.

Rank released games by one source of player ratings

TOPómetro (UC-018): one position per game, ranked by the player ratings of exactly one source, never a blend of sources. PostgreSQL selects the games that hold a usable score from that source and a release that has effectively occurred under the rating eligibility rules, then orders them by the unrounded mean descending, the number of ratings behind it descending and the unique gameId ascending, counts them and pages them. A game without a score from the source is not ranked and never counts as zero. An IGDB players' score is ranked only from the operator's minimum number of ratings on (50 by default); a community score from the operator's minimum on (1 by default) and states its count (UC-024). position is the game's place in that one sequence, so the first page's first three items are the podium and later pages continue it. Scores change independently of the catalogue, so a game may move between two page reads; a client that reads several pages keeps the first occurrence of a gameId. It never varies on the session or preferred platforms and never calls a provider.

Since 5.5.0, platformIds scopes the ranking to games released on those platforms (RNK-005): only a release on one of them that proves rating eligibility at the evaluation date makes a game a candidate, so a game released elsewhere years before is not ranked on a platform until it has effectively come out there. The scope is applied before ordering, counting and paging, never to a page of the global ranking. Each game still appears once and keeps its global score from the source: no per-platform score or mean is ranked or shown. Each scoped item adds platformRelease, the release that presents the game on the scope at its own date precision. Without platformIds the ranking and its items are unchanged.

query Parameters
source
string (RankingSource)
Default: "igdb_players"
Enum: "igdb_players" "gameometro_community"
Example: source=gameometro_community

The one population whose ratings rank the games. igdb_players is the IGDB players' rating mean and count stored locally with each game (ExternalPlayerScore), ranked only when the operator's minimum number of ratings stands behind it (50 by default); it is the default because it covers most games. gameometro_community is the Gameómetro community mean of one contribution per rating and its number of ratings, ranked from the operator's minimum (the first rating by default). Sources are never combined, and critic or combined provider scores are never used.

platformIds
Array of strings (PlatformId) <= 50 items unique [ items [ 1 .. 100 ] characters ]
Example: platformIds=platform_ps5&platformIds=platform_switch2

Repeatable platform restriction (platformIds=a&platformIds=b) applied before ranking: values combine with OR. Omit it for every platform. Values are trimmed and de-duplicated; an unknown value yields 422 PLATFORM_NOT_SUPPORTED.

page
integer >= 1
Default: 1
Example: page=1

One-based page; a page beyond the last returns an empty page.

pageSize
integer [ 1 .. 100 ]
Default: 20
Example: pageSize=20
header Parameters
If-None-Match
string
Example: "catalogue-version-opaque"

Opaque public representation tag for a conditional read.

Platform catalogue

Public browsing of every locally known game of one platform or platform family, without a search query.

Browse the local catalogue of one platform

Explorar catálogo (UC-019): a bounded page of the games of the last valid local catalogue publication that hold a release on any of the requested platforms, without a search query. A platform family such as Xbox Series X|S or a featured platform is sent as the product platform identifiers it groups; no platform entity is invented for it. Cancelled releases never associate a game with a platform.

Each game appears once, whatever its releases and regions on those platforms, and carries one platformRelease: the release of the platform scope that presents it. A game with a release that has effectively occurred at the evaluation date (Europe/Madrid) is presented by one of those releases; otherwise by an expected release with a known date, otherwise by a delayed or undated one. Occurrence derives from the effective date under the same rule as game details (an exact day from that day on, a month, quarter or year once it has ended, an unknown date only with explicit released evidence), never from a stored status, and delayed evidence never occurs. Within that class the presentation precedence of ReleaseItem chooses, ending with the earliest date and releaseId. Its status is therefore released exactly for the games releaseState=released selects; scheduled, announced (unknown date) and delayed are the games still to come, and cancelled never appears. The date keeps its real precision and is never narrowed to an invented day.

q optionally narrows the scope to games whose canonical title or an approved alias matches under the searchGames rules (normalized, all tokens, word prefixes, non-fuzzy); it filters and never reorders. releaseState, the inclusive year range on the presented release's known year and genreIds (OR within the dimension) combine with AND. A year range excludes a presented release with an unknown date. availableFilters is faceted: its genres are those of the games matching every other active filter, never narrowed by the active genre selection, and a selected genre always stays representable; its years span the presented releases matching every filter except the year range.

PostgreSQL selects, deduplicates, presents, filters, counts, orders and pages the games before the page reaches the application. Scores, genres and the matched alias are read for the returned page only. The total counts games, not releases, and makes no claim of exhaustive historical coverage. It never varies on the session or preferred platforms and never calls a provider.

query Parameters
platformIds
required
Array of strings (PlatformId) [ 1 .. 20 ] items unique [ items [ 1 .. 100 ] characters ]
Example: platformIds=platform_switch2

Repeatable platform scope (platformIds=a&platformIds=b): the product platform identifiers of one platform or one platform family, combined with OR. At least one is required: without it the request is malformed (400 REQUEST_MALFORMED). Values are trimmed and de-duplicated; an unknown value yields 422 PLATFORM_NOT_SUPPORTED.

q
string [ 1 .. 100 ] characters .*\S.*
Example: q=zelda

Optional title search inside the platform scope, trimmed, with 1 to 100 Unicode code points. A query whose normalized form holds no token yields 422 SEARCH_QUERY_INVALID.

releaseState
string (PlatformGameReleaseState)
Enum: "released" "upcoming"
Example: releaseState=upcoming

Omit it for every game of the scope. released keeps the games whose presented release has effectively occurred at the evaluation date; upcoming keeps the others: expected, delayed or still undated.

fromYear
integer <int32> [ 1 .. 9999 ]
Example: fromYear=2026

First calendar year, inclusive, of the presented release's known date. Either bound may be sent alone; a fromYear after toYear yields 422 FILTER_INVALID for /query/toYear.

toYear
integer <int32> [ 1 .. 9999 ]
Example: toYear=2027

Last calendar year, inclusive, of the presented release's known date.

genreIds
Array of strings (GenreId) <= 30 items unique [ items [ 1 .. 100 ] characters ]
Example: genreIds=genre_adventure

Repeatable multi-select genre filter (genreIds=a&genreIds=b) over the existing localized product genres; values combine with OR. Values are trimmed and de-duplicated; an unknown value yields 422 FILTER_INVALID for /query/genreIds.

sort
string (PlatformGamesSort)
Default: "release_date_desc"
Enum: "release_date_desc" "release_date_asc" "title_asc" "title_desc" "community_score" "external_player_score"
Example: sort=release_date_asc

The order of the games, applied before pagination; every order ends in the unique gameId. The date orders position each game by its presented release: the last day of its known period (the day itself for an exact date), then an exact day before a month, quarter or year ending the same day, then the normalized canonical title. A presented release with an unknown date follows every dated one in both directions and is never treated as a date. release_date_desc (the default) puts the latest first, release_date_asc the earliest. The title orders use the normalized canonical title. community_score puts the highest Gameómetro community mean, at the one decimal shown, first, then more ratings; external_player_score the highest stored external player score (currently IGDB players) at the one decimal of its /10 value, then more of that source's ratings. A game without the chosen score follows every game with one and is never treated as zero; ties continue with release_date_desc.

page
integer >= 1
Default: 1
Example: page=1

One-based page; a page beyond the last returns an empty page.

pageSize
integer [ 1 .. 100 ]
Default: 20
Example: pageSize=20
header Parameters
If-None-Match
string
Example: "catalogue-version-opaque"

Opaque public representation tag for a conditional read.

Upcoming highlights

Public ranking of one platform's most anticipated upcoming games by locally observed attention (Próximos destacados), never by quality.

Rank the most anticipated upcoming games of one platform

Próximos destacados (UC-020): at most ten distinct games of the last valid local catalogue publication that are still to come on the requested platform scope inside a moving horizon of the operator's calendar months (UC-024, six by default), ranked by release attention over the horizon (the ReleaseSort hype order, since 5.14.0) descending, then gameId ascending. A platform family is sent as the product platform identifiers it groups, as for browsePlatformGames; no platform entity is invented for it.

The application derives the evaluation date in Europe/Madrid. The horizon (window) starts on it and ends on the day before the same day of the month that many calendar months later; when that day does not exist, it ends on the last day of that month (from 31 August to 28 February; in a leap year to 29 February). The visitor never chooses the dates.

A release qualifies on a scope platform when it is a launch (stage full_release, or unknown since 5.14.0), neither cancelled nor delayed nor pending review, and its known date can only fall inside the horizon and after the evaluation date: an exact day after the evaluation date and no later than window.to, or a month or quarter that has not ended and ends no later than window.to. A year or unknown (TBA) date never qualifies, and no date is narrowed to an invented day. A game is a candidate when it has a qualifying release on the scope, no release on the scope that has already effectively occurred (the browsePlatformGames occurrence rule, so released and upcoming agree with Explorar catálogo), and is not known to be an edition rather than a distinct product. A game already released on another platform may be a candidate: what matters is that it is new to this platform. Only candidates with an attention signal are ranked; a candidate without one is not ranked and no value is ever invented.

Each item presents one qualifying release of the scope, chosen by the ReleaseItem presentation precedence with the earliest date first, and carries the landscape image of FeaturedImage: the first item uses the hero policy, the others the card policy. Attention combines provider-observed interest with the operator's editorial anticipation lists: never quality, a rating or a community opinion, and the value itself is not exposed. The selection never claims that the local catalogue holds every release of the platform. PostgreSQL selects, deduplicates, ranks and limits the games and presents their release before anything reaches the application. It never varies on the session or preferred platforms and never calls a provider.

query Parameters
platformIds
required
Array of strings (PlatformId) [ 1 .. 20 ] items unique [ items [ 1 .. 100 ] characters ]
Example: platformIds=platform_switch2

Repeatable platform scope (platformIds=a&platformIds=b): the product platform identifiers of one platform or one platform family, combined with OR. At least one is required: without it the request is malformed (400 REQUEST_MALFORMED). Values are trimmed and de-duplicated; an unknown value yields 422 PLATFORM_NOT_SUPPORTED.

header Parameters
If-None-Match
string
Example: "catalogue-version-opaque"

Opaque public representation tag for a conditional read.

Read minimal BFF session state

Terminate the current BFF session

Invalidates the opaque application session immediately. To also end this browser's identity-provider session, the client then navigates the top-level browsing context to the /auth/logout authentication route: it redirects once through the provider's standard OIDC end-session endpoint, which returns the browser to the application root. Other sessions, including the same account's on other devices, are unaffected. The response never contains a token; the ended session's ID token travels only in that redirect, as the standard id_token_hint. Without the navigation, only the application session ends.

Catalogue administration

Catalogue acquisition for sessions holding the catalogue operator authority: reads of local run and coverage evidence, a command that requests a bounded synchronization and returns before any provider work, and commands that stop or abandon one identified run. No operation here waits for, or exposes, the provider.

Read the current synchronization run and bounded recent run history

Requires an authenticated session holding the catalogue operator authority. Returns the run that currently holds synchronization ownership, when one exists, and at most twenty finished runs that bounded run history still retains, newest first. Run history is operational evidence, not coverage: a failed, interrupted, abandoned or partial run never changes coverage, and a run pruned from history keeps the coverage it recorded. Counters are absent, never zero, for a run that reported none. No provider payload, credential, provider identifier or internal topology is returned, and the read never calls the provider.

Request one bounded synchronization of an inclusive release-date interval

Requires an authenticated session holding the catalogue operator authority and its session-bound CSRF token. Validates the inclusive from–to interval, takes the single synchronization ownership and answers 202 with the accepted run before any provider work begins; the run continues in the background. Follow it with GET /admin/catalogue/synchronization: the accepted runId is the currentRun while it runs and then appears in recentRuns with its result. The run is the same synchronization and reconciliation as every other trigger, and its coverage follows the same rules.

Only one synchronization runs at a time, whatever started it: while another run holds ownership the request is rejected with 409 SYNCHRONIZATION_ALREADY_RUNNING and starts nothing. An environment without provider access rejects it with 422 SYNCHRONIZATION_DISABLED. The interval is at most 184 days, any calendar half-year, between 1950-01-01 and 2099-12-31; longer historical backfill is a separate, resumable operator workflow. Nothing is retried automatically, and the response never carries a provider payload, credential, provider identifier or internal topology.

Request a cooperative stop of the identified synchronization run

Requires an authenticated session holding the catalogue operator authority and its session-bound CSRF token. Records a stop request on the run named by runId, never on whichever run happens to be in flight, and answers 202 at once. The worker keeps running until its next safe point, before its next provider page or Game, so the current provider call and Game write finish first under their own timeouts; nothing is killed and no transaction is interrupted. Follow the run with GET /admin/catalogue/synchronization: it shows stopRequestedAt while it runs and then appears in recentRuns.

A run that reaches a safe point finishes with outcome code SYNCHRONIZATION_STOPPED: partial when it committed Games, which stay committed, otherwise failed. It never records coverage of its interval, and coverage recorded earlier stays in place. A run that finishes before reaching a safe point keeps its ordinary result, still showing stopRequestedAt. A stop never retries the run and never changes recurring schedules. Repeating the request for the same run in flight answers the first request's time. A finished run is 409 SYNCHRONIZATION_RUN_FINISHED and a run that history does not hold is 404 SYNCHRONIZATION_RUN_NOT_FOUND; neither changes anything.

Abandon the identified run when its worker no longer proves it is alive

Requires an authenticated session holding the catalogue operator authority and its session-bound CSRF token. An exceptional recovery for a run whose worker has stopped giving heartbeats, for example after the application stopped mid-run: the run named by runId is abandoned only while it still holds synchronization ownership and its last heartbeat is older than the configured abandonment period, the same evidence that reports it stalled and that lets the next run start take its ownership over. That check and the abandonment are one database statement serialized with the worker's own heartbeats, so a worker that proves it is alive meanwhile keeps its run.

Abandonment fences the run: from that moment its worker, if it resumes, cannot commit another Game, record coverage or finish the run, and it gives up at its next safe point. Games it already committed stay committed; nothing is rolled back. The run is answered at once as finished with result abandoned and outcome code SYNCHRONIZATION_ABANDONED_BY_OPERATOR, distinct from SYNCHRONIZATION_ABANDONED, which a later run start records, and ownership is free for the next run. Nothing is retried and recurring schedules do not change.

A run whose heartbeat is within the abandonment period is 409 SYNCHRONIZATION_RUN_NOT_STALE: request its stop instead. A finished run, including one already abandoned, is 409 SYNCHRONIZATION_RUN_FINISHED, and a run that history does not hold is 404 SYNCHRONIZATION_RUN_NOT_FOUND; none of them changes anything.

Read durable synchronization coverage of an inclusive release-date range

Requires an authenticated session holding the catalogue operator authority. Answers the inclusive from–to release-date range as consecutive periods in date order, each either covered or never_covered. A covered period was completely scanned by a synchronization run at a known time; that time is freshness evidence for the client's own presentation policy, never a claim that provider data cannot change later. Nothing becomes stale on the server. A period's failedGames is the covering run's own count of Games that kept their last valid state; it describes the whole run, not that period. PostgreSQL reads at most five hundred stored intervals, so one answer holds at most 1001 periods whatever the range length. A longer answer ends the day before continuesFrom, from which the client may ask again. The read never calls the provider.

required

Last day of the inclusive range; it must not precede from.

Editorial attention

The catalogue operator's editorial anticipation lists (UC-021): the prompt a language model answers with an editorial file, its preview against the catalogue, and the loaded lists whose 1–100 scores rank release attention together with the provider signals.

Read the editorial anticipation prompt and the loaded lists

Requires an authenticated session holding the catalogue operator authority (UC-021). Returns the versioned prompt an operator gives a language model with web access to obtain an editorial anticipation file, and at most 36 loaded lists, latest range first. In prompt.template, {{FROM}} and {{TO}} stand for the first and last ISO day of the range; the client substitutes them. Lists never overlap: every day belongs to at most one list. Nothing here reads the provider.

Preview how an editorial anticipation file would load

Requires the catalogue operator authority and session-bound CSRF proof. Reads the file text as the language model returned it (a surrounding Markdown code fence is tolerated, and members the schema does not name are ignored), validates it and matches every entry to a catalogued game: by the IGDB page slug first, else by a title exactly one catalogued game carries. Each entry states its match and warnings, and the preview names the list with the same range that loading would replace and any other list it overlaps. Nothing is stored.

Authorizations:
sessionCookie
header Parameters
X-CSRF-Token
required
string non-empty
Example: opaque-csrf-token

Session-bound anti-forgery token obtained from /session.

Request Body schema: application/json
required
content
required
string [ 1 .. 200000 ] characters

The file text exactly as the language model returned it. Version 1 of the file is a JSON object with schemaVersion 1, range (from, to, inclusive ISO days, at most 92 days), generatedAt, generator (prompt, model) and 1 to 50 entries, each with a unique rank (1–50), igdbSlug (or null), title, releaseDate (or null), an integer score (1–100), rationale (at most 500 characters) and at most 10 sources. The prompt template states it in full.

Responses

Same-origin application deployment

Load an editorial anticipation file as the list of its range

Requires the catalogue operator authority and session-bound CSRF proof. Validates and matches the file as the preview does, then applies the operator's assignments: each names an entry by rank and either a catalogued game, which replaces the automatic match, or none, which leaves the entry out. Entries without a game are left out, and a game named twice keeps its highest score. The list replaces the list with exactly the same range in one transaction; a list overlapping the range otherwise is refused with 409 and nothing changes. From the next read on, the release attention of every range overlapping the list includes its scores.

Product settings

The catalogue operator's product settings (UC-024): the closed, typed list of presentation and ranking values the operator may change without a restart or deployment, each with its default, range and origin, how the presentation windows compare with the configured acquisition horizon, and the recent audited changes. Secrets, endpoints, schedules and safety bounds are never editable here.

Read the operator-editable product settings

Requires an authenticated session holding the catalogue operator authority. Returns every registered setting with its effective value, default, inclusive range and origin, the settings revision an update must name, how the featured and upcoming presentation windows compare with the configured acquisition horizon, and at most 30 recent changes, newest first. Nothing here reads the provider.

Change product settings

Requires the catalogue operator authority and session-bound CSRF proof. Applies every change, or none: each names a registered setting once and either a new value inside its range and kind or no value, which restores the default. The resulting settings must keep at least one positive provider attention weight and strictly ascending calendar interest thresholds. revision is the revision the changes were prepared from; when another change came first the update is refused with 409 and nothing changes. Each accepted change is audited with the authenticated operator, its time and its previous and new effective values, and public reads use it from their next request on. A wider synchronization window applies from the next scheduled run; nothing requests provider work now.
